segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Hi Dana, thanks for making the time. I had us down for a quick review of the 35-seat quote and the January rollout timing. Does that still work?

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Yeah, that works. We reviewed it internally, and the seat count is right for now. It would be 28 standard users and 7 managers.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Perfect. The proposal I sent has 35 total seats at $62 per seat per month, billed annually, so $26,040 for the first year. Implementation is the fixed $4,800 package.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. Finance asked if the invoice can be dated January 2nd instead of December. Our budget opens then.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, that's fine. We can set the contract effective date as January 2nd and target go-live for February 5th, assuming we get the signed order by December 18th.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That timeline is reasonable. For implementation, is that three training sessions or two?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: It includes two admin sessions and three end-user sessions, all remote. If you need one extra manager session later, we can add it for $750, but most teams don't need it.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Got it. Legal had one note on the auto-renewal. They want 60 days' notice instead of 90.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, we can accept 60 days. I'll update that language and send the revised order form this afternoon.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. Send it to me and copy Martin in procurement. If everything matches, we should be able to sign next week.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. I'll include the pricing summary, the January 2nd invoice note, and the February 5th go-live plan in the email.
